# Sirach Chapter 41 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 41 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_041_page_001.jpg

---

41:1 O death, how bitter is the memory of you to a man who is at peace in his possessions, to a man who has no distractions and is prosperous in all things, and still has the strength to enjoy food!

41:2 O death, how good is your judgment to a man who is in need and who fails in strength, who is very old and distracted by everything, and has no patience — and to one who despairs over his hope!

41:3 Do not fear the decree of death; remember those who went before you and those who will come after you. This is the decree from the Lord upon all flesh.

41:4 And why do you set yourself against the good pleasure of the Most High? Whether it is ten or a hundred or a thousand years — there is no inquiry about life in Hades.

41:5 The children of sinners are abominable children, and they frequent the dwellings of the ungodly.

41:6 The inheritance of the children of sinners will perish, and reproach will be constant upon their seed.

41:7 Children curse a father who is ungodly, because they are reproached on his account.

41:8 Woe to you, O ungodly men, who have forsaken the law of the Most High God!

41:9 When you are born, you are born to a curse; and when you die, a curse is your portion.

41:10 Whatever is of the earth returns to the earth, so the ungodly go from a curse to destruction.

41:11 The mourning of men is about their body, but the bad name of sinners will be wiped out.

41:12 Have regard for your name, for it will remain with you longer than a thousand great treasuries of gold.

41:13 The number of the days of a good life is few, but a good name endures forever.

41:14 My children, take hold of instruction in peace; hidden wisdom and unseen treasure — what is the profit in either?

41:15 Better is the person who conceals his folly than the man who conceals his wisdom.

41:16 Therefore be ashamed of the following things I am about to speak, for it is not good to show partiality in every matter:

41:17 Be ashamed before a father and a mother of fornication, and before a ruler and a powerful person of a lie;

41:18 before a master and a mistress, of an offense; before a congregation and a people, of a lawless act;

41:19 before a partner and a friend, of injustice; and in the place where you dwell, of theft.

41:20 Be ashamed of the truth of God and his covenant, and of leaning upon your elbow at a meal;

41:21 of scorning when someone gives and takes away, and of silence before those who greet you;

41:22 of gazing at a woman who is a prostitute, and of turning away your face from a relative;

41:23 of taking away a portion and not giving back, and of fixing your eyes upon another man's wife;

41:24 of meddling with his maidservant — and do not approach her bed;

41:25 of abusive words before friends, and after you have given something, of reproaching;

41:26 of repeating and reporting what you have heard, and of revealing secrets.

41:27 Then you will be truly ashamed, and you will find favor with every person.
